BACKGROUND: RuntimeEngine._record_attempt sets AttemptBundle.transition_cause: none (scene unchanged), forced (staged handoff), timer, earned. Today 'timer' means only 'the deadline backstop (_apply_resolution_deadline_backstop in canonical_events.py) produced segments on the SAME turn the scene changed'. But _apply_authored_transition runs BEFORE the backstop in RuntimeEngine.turn, so that can never happen: 'timer' is unreachable. Intended meaning of timer: the player's own earned facts would NOT have opened the exit; the deadline backstop (which commits ready resolution events at turns_since_entry >= handoff_after_turns) is what made the authored transition available, and the exit then fired on this or a later turn of the same scene visit.

DESIGN CONSTRAINT FROM THE OWNER: do NOT add a mutable state flag (it can go stale). Derive the answer from immutable per-turn history instead. Implement exactly this:
1. state.py TurnRecord: add `deadline_event_ids: tuple[str, ...] = ()` (default empty so old saves still load; model stays frozen/extra=forbid). Event ids of resolution events the deadline backstop committed on that turn.
2. canonical_events.py: _apply_resolution_deadline_backstop must make the ids it committed available to the caller (for example return them beside the segments, or record them on a per-call local attribute that the caller reads immediately and that is overwritten at the start of every call; no value may survive to a later turn). Adjust the single caller in engine.py (and the second call site near resolve_break if the backstop is also used there; read it). _record_turn is called BEFORE the backstop in turn(): so after the backstop runs, replace the just-appended TurnRecord with a copy carrying deadline_event_ids (TurnRecord is frozen: use model_copy and assign into state.turn_records[-1]); keep the bounded list behaviour. Do this only when ids is non-empty.
3. engine.py _record_attempt: when the scene changed and not forced: compute `deadline_ids` = union of deadline_event_ids over the TurnRecords of the CURRENT scene visit, which are the last (before_turn_index_after_increment - scene_entered_at_turn_of_the_visit_being_left) records of state.turn_records, i.e. the records of turns played in the scene that was just left including this turn (use the pre-turn snapshot `before` for the left scene's entered turn and the post-turn turn_index; be careful: state.scene_entered_at_turn already changed after the transition). If deadline_ids is empty -> 'earned'. Otherwise evaluate the exit WITHOUT the backstop: take the transition that was taken (state.turn_records[-1].transition_id; if none, fall back to earned), look up its triggers, and test whether all triggers (predicate_matches, as in validation.eligible_transitions) hold on a COPY of the pre-exit facts from which the predicates asserted by those deadline events' operations (package.storylet_routes resolution_events[...].operations, op 'assert') were removed. If they do NOT all hold without those facts -> 'timer'; else 'earned'. Everything must be a pure read of immutable history plus the package; write no new state. A visit slice that is shorter than expected because of the 24-record bound must degrade to 'earned', never raise.
4. Update the _record_attempt docstring to say this. Keep forced as is. No story-specific names in runtime code.
5. Tests in tests/test_attempt_bundle.py, real package data (scenes with resolution events and transitions: read the package pacing transitions and storylet_routes resolution_events to find one scene where a transition trigger fact is established ONLY by a resolution event; if no real scene has that, say so in notes and build the closest real case by removing the player-earnable source of the trigger fact in the state): (a) test_deadline_backstop_then_exit_is_timer: a state at/after handoff_after_turns whose transition triggers are only satisfied once the backstop commits its resolution event; turn N runs the backstop (cause none, TurnRecord.deadline_event_ids non-empty), turn N+1 changes scene -> bundle cause 'timer'. (b) the earned 1A exit tests (existing) still earned. (c) save/restore round trip of a state containing a TurnRecord with deadline_event_ids, and loading a TurnRecord dict without the field. (d) staleness guard test: after a scene exit via timer, play into the NEXT scene and exit it by an earned transition; the second exit is 'earned' (records of the earlier visit must not leak in) - build with real data as far as possible, otherwise unit-test the visit slicing helper directly (factor the slice+evaluation into a small private helper method so it can be tested). (e) deadline_event_ids from a visit longer than 24 records degrades to earned without raising (unit-test the helper).
Keep existing tests passing; update one only if its expectation is the old unreachable-timer rule.
